How We Work

OEM/ODM machining from your drawings or samples. Review the quotation, approve the sample and agree the records to receive with your parts.

Key facts and preparation
Orders from
1 piece
Production time
7–14 business days

After drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing.

Transit time
Separate

Confirm shipping time for your destination and method.

Changes after approval
A drawing or quantity change requires an updated scope and schedule.

We can agree confidentiality terms before you send sensitive files. Use the checklist to prepare your requirements.

View RFQ checklist
Define the work
1. Define part requirements

Send your drawing or model and revision, material grade, quantity, required delivery date and part function.

Working from a sample? Explain the fit and function to retain or change, including any material changes. Agree the measurement and drawing work needed to define the part specification.

2. Review the quotation

Check the drawing revision against the quotation. Discuss tool access, workholding, mating features and critical requirements before agreeing to proposed geometry changes.

What your quotation covers
Machining & material
Drawing revision, grade, quantity, price and any agreed alternative.
Surface finishing
Included treatments and the surfaces to be controlled.
Inspection
Report scope, sampling and required records.
Separate charges
Tooling, special documentation, freight and duties where applicable.
Delivery terms
Production timing, shipping arrangements and responsibilities.
Machining capabilities
Approve before production
3. Check and approve the sample

Agree sample checks in advance: fit and appearance, critical interfaces and any defined functional tests.

Set the first-article review stage and release criteria. Record the drawing revision and approval criteria before moving to production.

4. Agree on batch inspection

Confirm the approved revision and checks for repeat production. Identify the features that need recorded results.

Agree material traceability requirements and the treatment of nonconforming parts. Our quality planning guide covers the records to request.

View quality planning guide
Prepare for handover
November 2022 LZZ packing archive. Customer, destination, carrier and export terms are not identified. These photographs do not define the packing for your order.
5. Arrange packing and shipment

Cartons or wooden cases depend on the parts and shipment requirements. Identify polished faces, sealing surfaces and vulnerable threads that need protection.

Specify labels, part numbers, drawing revision and quantity per pack where required. Provide the delivery address and receiving contact.

Distinguish the required arrival date from the planned dispatch date. Confirm the shipping method, Incoterm and responsibility for customs, duties and taxes.

Packing protection, transport costs and any arrival-date commitment must be agreed in your quotation.

6. Confirm documents for delivery

Use the approved drawing revision and order reference consistently for packing, shipment and inspection documents.

Specify the records needed with delivery, such as an agreed dimensional report or material documentation.

View factory workflow
If there is an issue

Send the drawing revision, part or batch reference, affected quantity, photographs and measurement details. We review the discrepancy against the agreed acceptance criteria and agree corrective action with you.

View available order documentation
